summary: Iteration 17: tested course content counts (backend + landing/courses cards + dialog) and the 60 new SOC challenges (API, table, difficulty column, combined filters, count, submit/grading, deep-link regression). Everything requested works. Backend 6/6 pytest pass. Frontend: all checks pass.

minor.issue: seed_collection only inserts challenges whose id is missing, and seed_data.py setdefault('difficulty') only changes the in-memory seed. If a database (e.g. production) already has the 5 original challenges without a difficulty field, they never get one. Their Difficulty cell is then blank and choosing any difficulty filter hides them. The preview DB already has difficulty on all 65, so I couldn't reproduce this here; it comes from reading the code. Fix: add a startup step that sets difficulty on challenges missing it, e.g. update_many({id, difficulty:{$exists:false}}, {$set:{difficulty}}).

Rule IDs are reused across unrelated alerts: SOC201 appears 6 times (e.g. 'User Reported Phishing Email' and 'SSH Brute Force Detected'), and SOC204, SOC215, SOC202 3 times each. This is cosmetic, but searching by rule returns mixed categories.

issues: The 'Solved' status filter and the 'N solved' count include any submission, even wrong-verdict 0/100 attempts. 'Attempted' would be a more accurate label, or count only verdict_correct submissions.
The subtitle still says 'Click a course to see the matching labs and drills'. This is correct for the dialog, so just noting it.

action_items: Add a startup step that backfills difficulty on existing challenge docs that lack it, so production DBs created before this change show and filter the 5 original challenges
Optional: give each of the 60 new challenges a unique rule ID
Optional: rename the 'Solved' filter to 'Attempted', or count only correct verdicts
critical_code_review_comments: routes_practice list_challenges uses to_list(200). That is fine for 65 challenges but will silently cut off past 200.
Verdict split is 45 TP / 15 FP, which is reasonable. Several FP keyword lists include the phrase 'false positive', which rewards writing the verdict in the report. That is acceptable.
contentLabel correctly returns an empty string when all counts are 0, and the dialog then falls back to c.type.
seed_data_creation: Demo student submitted challenge ch-02-2 (wrong verdict, 0/100) through the UI, plus one ch-02-x submission and a wrong-verdict submission on ch-01-2 through pytest (reports prefixed TEST_).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Course content counts verified against all 13 store IDs. Landing grid shows 8 cards and /courses shows 13. /app/challenges shows 65 rows, 12 categories plus 'All', and the Easy/Medium/Hard column. Filters combine correctly (Ransomware 6, Ransomware+Hard 2; Open + Solved = 65). The deep link ?case=ch-phish-01 opens the briefing and then the investigation.
